source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb (and glossary); 8.5; 9.4

main.t: A moon-shaped wrist bone in the middle of the first row of carpal bones (lunate).

simpler.t: The lunate is a small wrist bone in the middle of your wrist.

deeper.t: With the scaphoid, it is one of only two carpal bones that meet the radius directly.

facts.t: It is the second bone of the first (proximal) row, counting from the thumb side.
Above it is the radius. Below it are the capitate and hamate.
The scaphoid lies beside it on the thumb side, and the triquetrum on the little-finger side.

simpler.t: It sits in the middle of the wrist, just below the end of the radius.

deeper.t: Only three carpal bones take part in the wrist joint: the scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum.

items.name: Surface for the radius
items.t: Its upper surface meets the radius directly at the wrist joint.

items.name: Surfaces for the second row
items.t: Its lower surface meets the capitate and hamate at the midcarpal joint.

items.name: Side surfaces
items.t: It meets the scaphoid on the thumb side and the triquetrum on the other.

simpler.t: It is a small curved bone with joints on four sides.

deeper.t: Ligaments unite it with the other three bones of its row, so they work as one unit.

facts.t: Its upper surface meets the radius, so it shares the wrist joint with the scaphoid.
Its lower surface takes part in the midcarpal joint. The two joints together make all wrist movements.
With the other carpal bones it forms the walls and floor of the carpal tunnel.

simpler.t: It is one of the bones the wrist bends on.

items.name: Wrist (radiocarpal) joint
items.t: A condyloid joint: the lunate and scaphoid meet the radius.

items.name: Midcarpal joint
items.t: Its lower surface meets the capitate and hamate.

items.name: Scaphoid and triquetrum
items.t: Its neighbours in the first row, joined to it by ligaments.

items.name: Carpal tunnel
items.t: The carpal bones form its walls and floor.

items.name: Median nerve
items.t: Runs through the carpal tunnel, in front of the lunate.

simpler.t: It joins the radius above, the second row below and its two neighbours at the sides.

facts.t: It forms by replacing a cartilage model with bone (endochondral ossification), like all limb bones except the clavicle.
Its single ossification centre appears at about the fifth year.
facts.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20). Gray’s 1918 (8.2) gives the fifth year (supporting only).

items.injury: Overuse of the tendons or a wrist injury makes the contents of the carpal tunnel swell.
items.damaged: The nerve in the tunnel, whose walls and floor the carpal bones form.
items.cannotDo: Use the hand without pain, numbness or weakness (carpal tunnel syndrome).
items.why: The bony walls and floor and the tough roof cannot stretch, so swelling presses on the nerve.

items.injury: A fall onto the outstretched hand with the wrist bent far back.
items.damaged: The lunate dislocates forwards, into the carpal tunnel.
items.cannotDo: Feel the thumb, index and middle fingers normally.
items.why: The dislocated bone takes up space in the tunnel and presses on the median nerve.

items.q: Explain which carpal bones form the wrist joint, and how.
model: Three carpal bones take part: the scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum.
The scaphoid and lunate meet the radius directly.
The triquetrum meets the articular disc over the ulna.
The ulna itself does not touch the carpal bones.

items.q: Compare the lunate and the scaphoid.
model: Both are in the first row, and both meet the radius directly.
The scaphoid is boat-shaped and outermost, on the thumb side.
The lunate is moon-shaped and second from the thumb side.
The scaphoid is the carpal bone broken most often.

items.q: Predict the effect of the lunate dislocating forwards into the carpal tunnel.
model: It takes up space in the tunnel.
It presses on the median nerve.
Numbness of the thumb, index and middle fingers.
Weakness of the small muscles of the thumb.

check.stem: Which bones meet the lower surface of the lunate?
check.why: Its lower surface meets the capitate and hamate at the midcarpal joint.

check.stem: Which two carpal bones meet the radius directly?
check.why: The scaphoid and lunate meet the radius; the triquetrum meets the articular disc over the ulna.
